clue.text: Nobel Peace prize winner breaching royal protocol?

definitions.meaning: Henry ..., US Secretary of State, shared the 1973 Nobel Peace Prize
read as ..., planting a kiss on the Queen, which etiquette forbids

explanation.surface: A distinguished laureate commits a faux pas in front of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the name as KISSING ER: ER is the late Queen (Elizabeth Regina), and nobody is meant to kiss her. The question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger, the American diplomat, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1973 for the Vietnam ceasefire talks.

clue.text: One in ten make blunders delivering anaesthetic

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
blunders means makes a mess of, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One in ten anaesthetists makes a mistake during delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' rearranges TEN MAKE into KETAMNE; 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketamine is a drug used as a general anaesthetic, especially in veterinary practice.

clue.text: That lady, Wimbledon champion in the 70s, is going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter in a down answer

parts.note: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975

explanation.surface: A female tennis star of the seventies appears without her top.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the pronoun used for a woman already mentioned.

clue.text: Climbing equipment made by team of gelato sellers?

indicators.note: team of the ice trade puts ICES before CREW in the answer

parts.note: read as ICE'S, the ice-cream trade's; ices are frozen desserts such as gelato
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: Mountaineering gear produced by a gang of ice-cream vendors.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a fanciful respacing of the answer as a possessive: the frozen-dessert trade's team.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice screw is a threaded metal tube screwed into ice as protection when climbing.

clue.text: My turn, be quiet

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
SH is the command to hush

explanation.surface: A player says it is their turn and asks for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, used interchangeably.

clue.text: Subjugation of announcement about replacing former partner

indicators.note: replacing says one element takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: an expression is a statement or utterance
an ex is a former partner
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A press statement concerning a new partner talks of oppression.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is the forcible subduing of people, much like subjugation.

clue.text: Barbarian leader from part of Greece left for Carthage originally

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Attica is the region of Greece around Athens

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient warlord from a Greek region heads off to Carthage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads like 'departed', but it is L, put in place of C ('Carthage originally').
explanation.definitionFit: Attila was the fifth-century leader of the Huns, a byword for barbarian invaders.

clue.text: Extent of English desire for too much cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

parts.note: greed is excessive desire

explanation.surface: How far English greed goes when out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the D of EGREED from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Degree means extent or level, as in 'to a degree'.

clue.text: European visiting Great Lake's restaurant?

parts.note: visiting someone means being at their place, so AT
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A traveller from Europe drops in at a lakeside diner in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the unusual spelling: EATERIE, with the lake's ending, for the usual 'eatery'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery is an informal restaurant; this spelling is a recognised variant.

clue.text: Mostly estimate charges to go round North Korea?

indicators.note: charges means rushes in, so one piece barges into the other

parts.note: to rotate is to go round

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a guess is a rough estimate

explanation.surface: An estimate of fees for a round trip to North Korea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like fees but is the verb 'rushes in', putting one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is often called a rogue state, one seen as defying international law; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Article uses works to portray mythical king

parts.note: THE is the definite article

indicators.note: works in the sense of kneads or reshapes, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An essay draws on artworks to depict a legendary monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges USES into SEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus, slayer of the Minotaur, was the legendary ruler of Athens in Greek myth.

clue.text: Messenger baring her bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters before it are messed up

explanation.surface: A courier moons the recipient, exposing her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a noun for a backside but works as the adjective 'poor quality', signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a herald or forerunner announcing something to come.

clue.text: Vindictiveness of male child at tea-party?

parts.note: Alice attends the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A boy turns spiteful at a children's party.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm others, ill will close to vindictive spite.

clue.text: I try and signal nasty swelling of organ

indicators.note: nasty means badly made, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tries to warn of a painful inflammation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges I TRY SIGNAL; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx, the voice box.

clue.text: Amble around when feeding small child crispy bread

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are rearranged
feeding means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Wandering about while giving a toddler some crunchy toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' standing for AS is a common crossword equivalence ('as I left' = 'when I left').
explanation.definitionFit: Melba toast is very thin, dry toast, named after the singer Nellie Melba.

clue.text: View capturing a lake with sides of different length

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a scene is a view or vista
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A landscape painting includes a lake with uneven shores.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle has three unequal sides, a geometry term.

clue.text: School second XI backed to restrict runs, being calm and collected

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the next piece sits inside the reversed letters
backed means sent backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football team
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A school's reserve cricket team keeps the scoring down and stays unruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SSELEVEN into NEVELESS; 'to restrict' then puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nerveless means showing no nervousness, staying cool under pressure.

clue.text: British rock band with uplifting musical style is not up to scratch

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra

indicators.note: uplifting means lifting up, so in a down answer the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: rap is a musical genre

explanation.surface: A British rock group with an upbeat sound is mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Below par means below the usual standard, from golf's par score.

clue.text: Working is stopping elderly being worried

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: aged means elderly
on means working, as in a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Pensioners fret about still having to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means anguished or tormented by anxiety.

clue.text: Embargo on adapted missile

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An arms embargo is placed on a modified weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges EMBARGO ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing stick, a missile that can return to the thrower.

clue.text: Retiring billionaire Glaswegian suppresses nation

indicators.note: Retiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
suppresses means keeps out of sight, so the letters lie concealed inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wealthy Scot steps down and keeps a whole country under his thumb.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'suppresses nation' as the definition, but 'suppresses' is the signal that the letters are concealed in 'billionaire Glaswegian'; the definition is 'nation' alone. 'Retiring' reads AIREGLA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African country, the largest in Africa by area.

clue.text: A booty shake, say, in the office?

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is spoken, words sounding like the answer

parts.note: a twerk is a dance shaking the bottom, so A TWERK

explanation.surface: An office worker bursts into a provocative dance at their desk.
explanation.walkthrough: A TWERK, said out loud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at work means being on the job, typically in the office; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Keen, raising energy to get wasted

indicators.note: wasted means lost, so that letter disappears

parts.note: rearing children means raising them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Parenting so exhausting it drives you to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' suggests drunkenness but here means the E is used up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in 'raring to go', means very eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Gabon divided by introduction of Nazi rule

parts.note: G is Gabon's international vehicle registration code
in a fraction one number is written over another, so divided by is OVER

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An African country is split by the arrival of fascism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' reads like a split, but in arithmetic 'six over two' means six divided by two.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or control a country or people.

clue.text: Dilute effect of harrowing story of rabbits abandoning ship

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that word is dropped from the title

parts.note: Watership Down is Richard Adams's novel about rabbits, famous for its bleak, upsetting scenes
taken as written

explanation.surface: The impact of a grim rabbit tale is softened once the sailors leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To water down something is to weaken it or make it less forceful.

clue.text: Zip code's ending in river

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing, nil

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The end of a postal code lies in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip code' looks like the US postcode, but Zip means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Hinders one million couples

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
couples are pairs

explanation.surface: A million married couples get in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Impairs means damages or weakens, which hampers how something works.

clue.text: American released from islands belonging to the aforementioned

indicators.note: released from means let out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: an ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A US prisoner is freed from island confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Its is the possessive pronoun for a thing just mentioned.

clue.text: Is bitter about Conservatives abandoning representations of Islam?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: the crescent moon is a common emblem of Islam
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, so two Conservatives are two Cs

explanation.surface: Someone resents the Tories dropping religious symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Cs leave from separate places: the start and the middle of CRESCENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation about it.

clue.text: Speculated that half-cut lust, in retrospect, limits love

indicators.note: half-cut means only part of the word is kept, here its first two letters
limits means encloses within bounds, so one piece holds the other
in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: lust is strong desire
O is love, the tennis score of zero

explanation.surface: A tipsy theorist wonders whether lust, looking back, constrains love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is slang for drunk but here keeps half of THAT. 'in retrospect' turns lust's synonym into ERISED, which 'limits' wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas or hypotheses, that is, to speculate.
